• Discuss the changes that occur to milk during UHT processing. [K] / [CO2]
  • UHT processing does not cause reduction in biological value of proteins. There is only

questions.question: Explain the method of drying foods in a Fluidised Bed Dryers. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the method of drying foods in a Fluidised Bed Dryers. [U] / [CO2]
  • In these driers hot air is blown through a food bed contained in metal trays with mesh
  • or perforated bases. The greater air velocities make the bed expand, and the food
  • particles become suspended in air and vigorously agitated. The bed is said to be
  • fluidised. The air thus acts as with the drying and the fluidising medium. Fluidising is
  • a very effective way of maximising the surface area of food for drying in a relatively
  • small space.

questions.question: Define fermentation of foods. Discuss the mechanisms of preservation in fermented foods. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define fermentation of foods. Discuss the mechanisms of preservation in
  • fermented foods. [U] / [CO3]
  • Fermentation is a biological process in which microorganisms such as bacteria, yeasts,
  • or molds convert sugars and other carbohydrates present in food into acids, alcohol, and
  • gases under controlled conditions. These end products help preserve food by creating
  • an environment that inhibits the growth of spoilage and disease -causing
  • microorganisms.

  • by inhibiting microbial growth. Ethanol fermentation is the process in which glucose is
  • converted to ethanol and carbon dioxide. Ethanol fermentation is also known as
  • alcoholic fermentation that converts sugars such as glucose, fructose, and su crose into
  • energy (A TP), ethanol and carbon dioxide as by-products. One glucose molecule is
  • converted into two ethanol molecules and two carbon dioxide molecules. yeasts

  • an anaerobic process. Products – Beer, wine, bread etc.

questions.question: Discuss on Lactic Acid Fermented food products. / [CO3]

  • Pickle – It’s a product prepared by lactic acid bacteria (LAB) fermentation of sugar
  • present in pieces of fruits and vegetables. The prepared product is rich in Lactic acid
  • and only the beneficial bacteria that can tolerate lactic acid pH survive.
  • Sauerkraut – It is basically a finely cut cabbage that has been fermented by various
  • lactic acid bacteria. Sauerkraut usually has a long shelf life and a distinctive sour flavor.
  • Yogurt – Y ogurt is basically a fermented product prepared from milk. The main method
  • of producing yogurt is through the lactic acid fermentation of milk with harmless
  • bacteria. The primary ba cteria used are typically Lactobacillus bulgaricus and
  • Streptococcus thermophiles.

questions.question: Write a detailed note on the advantages and principles of food preservation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a detailed note on the advantages and principles of food preservation.
  • [U] / [CO1]
  • Increases shelf life – Preservation techniques slow down spoilage caused by
  • microorganisms, enzymes, and environmental factors, allowing food to be stored for
  • longer periods.
  • Reduces food wastage – By extending the usability of food, preservation helps
  • minimize losses during storage, transportation, and distribution.
  • Ensures food availability year-round – Seasonal foods (fruits, vegetables, etc.) can be
  • preserved and made available even during off-seasons.
  • Enhances food safety – Methods like heating, drying, and freezing help destroy or
  • inhibit harmful microorganisms, reducing the risk of foodborne illnesses.
  • Maintains nutritional value – Proper preservation techniques help retain essential
  • nutrients, especially when compared to spoiled or degraded food.
  • Facilitates storage and transport – Preserved foods are often easier to store, package,
  • and transport over long distances.
  • Adds variety to diet – Preservation methods such as fermentation and pickling create
  • new flavors and food products.
  • Economic benefits – Helps stabilize food prices, supports food industries, and provides
  • income opportunities through processed food products.

questions.question: Discuss the advantages of sterilized foods. Summarize the difference between pasteurization and sterilization process in foods. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Discuss the advantages of sterilized foods. Summarize the difference between pasteurization and sterilization process in foods. [U] / [CO2] Difference between Pasteurization and Sterilization Aspect Pasteurization Sterilization Definition Mild heat treatment used to destroy pathogenic microorganisms and reduce spoilage organisms Severe heat treatment used to destroy all microorganisms including spores Temperature Used Lower temperatures (generally below 100°C) Higher temperatures (usually above 100°C) Time Required Shorter time (seconds to minutes depending on method) Longer time or very high temperature for shorter time Microbial Destruction Kills pathogenic bacteria but not all spores Kills all microorganisms and spores Effect on Food Quality Minimal change in taste, color, and nutrients Greater changes in taste, texture, and some nutrients Shelf Life Extends shelf life but usually requires refrigeration Produces shelf -stable products that can be stored at room temperature Storage After Treatment Usually needs refrigeration Usually does not need refrigeration (if properly sealed)

questions.question: Write an essay on Refrigeration/Chilling of foods. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on Refrigeration/Chilling of foods. [U] / [CO2]
  • Refrigeration is one of the most important and widely used methods of food
  • preservation. It involves storing foods at low temperatures, us ually between 0°C and
  • 4°C, to slow down spoilage and maintain quality. By reducing temperature,
  • refrigeration delays the growth of microorganisms, slows enzymatic reactions, and
  • reduces chemical changes that cause food deterioration.
  • At low temperatures, t he activity of bacteria, yeasts, and molds is greatly reduced,
  • though not completely stopped. This helps in extending the shelf life of perishable foods
  • such as milk, meat, fish, fruits, vegetables, and cooked dishes. Enzyme activity, which
  • can lead to ripening and spoilage, is also slowed. As a result, color, flavor, texture, and
  • nutritional value are better preserved compared to storage at room temperature.
